stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec — no prior hand-curation. 'Live Preview of Content in CMS' is a complex, cross-cutting feature involving real-time rendering, content synchronization, and preview infrastructure across GO, UP, and MX. Openspec must run first to elaborate requirements, define AC, and propose technical depth; speckit then reviews openspec output to add testability criteria, security checks, and edge-case coverage. Priority high due to cross-platform scope and lack of any existing specification.

agentContributions.notes: Novel story: adding Contentstack Live Preview capability. Attachment points are the content context provider and the useContent hook that 236+ components depend on. The ContentstackContext must be extended to supply preview content; useContent must return preview-sourced data when preview is active. Acceptance criteria were empty, so VCs are derived from the description and the technical notes identifying the key integration files.

Openspec provided zero acceptance criteria, so all 17 criteria were derived from the story title, description, technical notes, and openspec's own notes about the integration points (ContentstackContext, useContent hook, ContentstackLink, contentCard interface, contentstack service). Criteria cover: functional behaviour (ACs 1-5), edge cases including null/missing and partial preview content (ACs 6-7), error handling for token expiry, API errors, and network failures (ACs 8-10), security including authorization gating, production-build isolation, and credential leakage prevention (ACs 11-13), cross-codeline consistency across GO/UP/MX (AC 14), performance non-regression for non-preview users and preview update latency (ACs 15-16), and accessibility parity in preview mode (AC 17). CAVEAT: File contents were not available for review — the actual implementations of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, and contentCard.ts may reveal additional integration constraints (e.g., specific content types that must support preview, routing patterns, SSR vs CSR rendering modes, or existing error-handling patterns) that could warrant additional criteria or refinement of existing ones. The criteria above represent the best derivation from available context.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents added meaningful, non-overlapping value: openspec identified the key integration points (ContentstackContext, useContent hook, ContentstackLink, contentCard interface, contentstack service) and derived verification criteria from the story description; speckit then built 17 comprehensive acceptance criteria from scratch covering functional behaviour, edge cases, security, cross-codeline consistency, performance, and accessibility. However, the story manifest provided does not contain a technicalNotes.files field, so there are no file paths to verify against the repository. The agents reference specific files in their notes (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, contentstack.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx, contentCard.ts) but these are not formalised in the manifest. Speckit explicitly flagged that file contents were not available for review, meaning the 17 derived ACs may miss implementation-specific constraints (content types, routing patterns, SSR vs CSR modes, existing error-handling patterns). A human reviewer should: (1) confirm whether technicalNotes.files should exist and populate it if so, (2) verify the referenced files exist in the repository, (3) review the 17 derived ACs against actual file implementations to catch integration constraints speckit could not see. This is a novel story with no prior hand-curation, so the collaborative pipeline was appropriate, but the output is not yet implementation-ready.
